title: Composition and Morphology Optimization of Macroporous Gelatin–Alginate Hydrogels
content: Macroporous gelatin–alginate hydrogels structured with poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether (PEGDE) and containing chlorhexidine (CHX) were investigated to determine how formulation affects pore geometry, a key factor governing fluid transport in porous wound-contacting materials. A two-factor response surface experiment comprised ten runs representing nine unique formulations and one replicated center-point composition. Two SEM images obtained from independent cross-sections were analyzed for each run. Each image was independently segmented using the Yen, Otsu, and Li thresholding algorithms, yielding 60 image-level morphometric analyses. Three pore descriptors were evaluated: 2D porosity, pore connectivity, and the largest connected pore area (LCPA). Regression models were selected using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). Although the thresholding methods produced substantial differences in absolute porosity values, all three segmentation approaches consistently identified the same favorable compositional trend: increasing PEGDE content and decreasing CHX content. The model-predicted favorable boundary region corresponded to 5.17 wt.% PEGDE and 0.61 wt.% CHX within the investigated design space. An additional validation series consisting of three formulations prepared under different freeze-drying and SEM-imaging conditions exhibited lower absolute porosity values but preserved the same qualitative composition–morphology relationship. Formulations combining high PEGDE content with low CHX content displayed the highest porosity and two-dimensional pore connectivity. These findings demonstrate a robust relationship between hydrogel composition and pore architecture while also highlighting the strong influence of freeze-drying conditions on the morphology of the resulting porous structures. The multi-threshold analysis further indicates that compositional trends are more reproducible than absolute morphometric values, supporting the use of multiple segmentation approaches for SEM-based optimization of porous hydrogel systems.
